Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi

On The 6 th Of August, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 827 of 2015
 Smt Alka Verma And Others
 Versus
Sourabh Gupta And Others
Appearance:
Shri Sourabh Neema, learned counsel for the appellants.

Shri Sudarshan Pandit, Advocate with Shri Rajesh Pandit  for respondent No.3 / Insurance Company.
 ORDER

The appellants have filed this Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved by the award dated 19.01.2015 passed by the Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Sarangpur, District Rajgarh (M.P.) in Claim Case No.86/2013.
2.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Sarangpur, District Rajgarh
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The factum of the accident and the liability of the Insurance Company are not in dispute.

3. The brief facts of the case are that on 07.02.2010 at around 10.00 PM, the deceased Sanjay Verma along with his friends Lakhan Jaiswal, Vinod Malviya and Sitaram was going from Sarangpur to Gwalior in their vehicle a Wagon R.

When they reached approximately 9 KM from Sarangpur, near the culvert at Dhanora, A.B. Road, respondent No.2 driving a Truck bearing registration number MP-09- HF-5974 came in a rash and negligent manner and rammed into the car of the deceased Sanjay Verma from the front.
All four persons in the car sustained grievous injuries.

They were immediately rushed to the Community Health NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:20903 2 MA-827-2015 Centre, Saragpur, but two of them, including Sanjay Verma succumbed to the injuries sustained in the accident.

entities.text: Community Health NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:20903 2 MA-827-2015 Centre
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
3.1. The appellants / claimants filed their claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 before the Claims Tribunal, which, after considering the evidence on record, assessed the loss of dependency at Rs.6,48,000/- and after awarding compensation under various heads, a total compensation of Rs.7,85,500/- was awarded to the appellants.
4. Counsel for the appellants submits that the Claims Tribunal wrongly disbelieved the claim of the appellants regarding the income of the deceased.

Referring to Exs.P-35 and P-36, he submits that, at Smt Alka Verma vs Sourabh Gupta on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172542966/
1 the time of accident, the deceased was working as a Supervisor in the employment of Babulal Porwal, a Government Civil Contractor of Tarana, District Ujjain.

By referring to the aforesaid documents, Ex.P-14, which is the licence of contractor and Ex.P-16, which is the attendance register of the deceased, it is clearly established that the appellant was working as a Supervisor for the aforesaid person.
He further submits that the salary register from September 2009 to January 2010 clearly shows that the appellant was receiving a salary of Rs.10,000/- per month.

Thus, he submits that the Claims Tribunal wrongly disbelieved the clear evidence brought on record in support of the claim regarding the income of the deceased and wrongly assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.4,500/- per month on notional basis.
4.1 He further submits that there are five claimants, the mother, father, wife, son and daughter of the deceased.
Thus, all five of them are entitled to compensation under the head of loss of consortium.
However, the Claims Tribunal awarded only Rs.1,00,000/-, whereas it should have been Rs.2,00,000/- i.e. Rs.40,000/- each for the five claimants.

In addition, he points out that for loss of estate, only a meager amount of Rs.2,500/- has been awarded and for funeral NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:20903 3 MA-827-2015 expenses, an amount of Rs.25,000/- has been awarded.

4.2 Learned counsel for the appellants also submits that, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi reported in 2017 ACJ 2700, the Claims Tribunal should have also added an amount to the income of the deceased for future prospects, which has not been done.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi reported in 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company supports the award and submits that considering the fact that a total sum of Rs.7,85,500/- has been awarded, no interference is required in the award.

He further submits that in fact for funeral expenses, in view of the ratio of Pranay Sethi (Supra) only an amount of Rs.15,000/- should have been awarded, but the Claims Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.25,000/-.

6. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
7.

On perusal of the attendance and salary registers enclosed as Exs.P-16 to P-40, it is seen that the appellants were able to establish the employment of the deceased as a Supervisor under the Government Contractor, Babulal Porwal.
It is clear from the record that not only the attendance register but also the salary payments for the month of September 2009 to January 2010 are available on record.
However, the details provided cover only a short duration of four months.

Thus,
in view of this fact, it would be reasonable to assess the salary of the deceased at Rs.7,500/- per month.

8. As regards the addition for future prospects, considering the age of the deceased (32 years) and in line with the findings of the Claims Tribunal in para 42, a 40% addition to the income of the deceased should be made, in accordance with the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (Supra) .

Smt Alka Verma vs Sourabh Gupta on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172542966/
2
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:20903 4 MA-827-2015 9.
As regards the loss of consortium

, in view of the fact that the claimants are the mother, father,
son, daughter and wife of the deceased, all five of them are entitled to compensation for loss of consortium at Rs.40,000/- each, which amounts to Rs.2,00,000/- in total.

10. As regards the funeral expenses, the amount is modified to Rs.15,000/- and for the loss of estate,
the amount is also modified to Rs.15,000/-.
As such, the total compensation would amount to Rs.17,42,000/-.

11. The Claims Tribunal has already awarded Rs.7,85,500/-, thus, the appellants are now entitled to additional compensation of Rs.9,56,500/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
12. The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the application before the Claims Tribunal.

13. It is seen from the record that the appeal is valued at Rs.5,00,000/- and thus, the appellants are directed to pay the deficit court fee within a period of four weeks from today.
14.
In view of the above, the present appeal is allowed.
Certified copy as per rules.
(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI)
